- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 74.23 → 75.71, 73.50 → 75.53).
- Underestimates prices in late forecast periods (last 5–10 days of 30d window), suggesting mean reversion or downward bias.
- Forecast lags behind true values by 1–3 days for most cases, particularly in mid-to-late periods.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent peaks.
- When history contains a strong downward trend, model fails to adjust downward, leading to overestimation.
- Model reacts too slowly to recent price drops; underestimates when true values are falling sharply.
- Forecast accuracy improves when history includes recent low prices, suggesting model is sensitive to recent volatility.
- Model tends to overcorrect after minor spikes, leading to overshoot followed by sharp correction.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are consistently too high, suggesting model lacks downward adjustment mechanism.
